translations.idiomatic: Wei Cao, whose style was Deyuan, came from Dai.

context.zh: 少通俠，有才略。

translations.literal: Jin General Who Pacifies the North Wei Guan made Cao a gate officer; he was repeatedly sent to the state and rather attached himself on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's General Who Pacifies the North, Wei Guan, appointed Cao gate officer and often sent him on missions to the Dai state, where Cao gradually built ties of his own.

context.zh: 始祖崩後，與從子雄及其宗室鄉親姬澹等十數人，同來歸國，說桓穆二帝招納晉人，於是晉人附者稍眾。

translations.literal: After the founding ancestor died, together with his nephew Xiong and more than ten clansmen and fellow-townsmen such as Ji Dan, he came in a body to return to the state, urging the Huan and Mu emperors to recruit Jin people; thereafter those of Jin who attached themselves grew somewhat numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding ancestor passed away, Cao came home with his nephew Xiong and a dozen-odd kinsmen and neighbors, among them Ji Dan, and urged the Huan and Mu emperors to welcome Jin subjects. From then on Jin adherents grew steadily in number.

context.zh: 桓帝嘉之，以為輔相，任以國事。

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan approved and named him chief minister, charging him with the affairs of the realm.

translations.literal: Pan Yue, style name Anren, was a man of Zhongmou in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue, courtesy name Anren, came from Zhongmou in Xingyang commandery.

units.zh: 陸機，字士衡，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Ji, courtesy name Shiheng, was a man of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji, whose courtesy name was Shiheng, came from Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 列傳第二十七 謝靈運

translations.literal: Biography 27: Xie Lingyun
translations.idiomatic: Biography 27: Xie Lingyun

units.zh: 謝靈運，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

units.zh: 祖玄，晉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan was General of Chariots and Cavalry of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan had been Jin's General of Chariots and Cavalry.

units.zh: 父瑍，生而不慧，為秘書郎，蚤亡。

translations.literal: His father Min was dull from birth, served as Secretary Gentleman, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Min had been slow-witted from childhood, held the post of Secretary Gentleman, and died young.

units.zh: 靈運幼便穎悟，玄甚異之，謂親知曰：「我乃生瑍，瑍那得生靈運！」

translations.literal: Lingyun as a child was already sharp and perceptive; Xuan greatly marveled at this and said to intimates, "I bore Min—how could Min have borne Lingyun!"
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun showed exceptional brilliance even as a boy. Xuan was astonished and told those close to him, "I fathered Min—how could Min have fathered Lingyun!"

units.zh: 靈運少好學，博覽群書，文章之美，江左莫逮。

translations.literal: Lingyun in youth loved learning, read widely among the classics, and in the beauty of his writing none south of the Yangzi could match him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Lingyun was devoted to study and read widely; in literary excellence none in the lands south of the Yangzi could rival him.

units.zh: 從叔混特知愛之，襲封康樂公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Hun especially knew and loved him; he inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Kangle with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Hun on his father's side took a special liking to him. He inherited the title Duke of Kangle, with a fief of three thousand households.

units.zh: 宣皇帝諱懿，字仲達，河內溫縣孝敬里人，姓司馬氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan's taboo name was Yi; his courtesy name was Zhongda. He was a native of Xiaojing Ward in Wen County in Henei, and his surname was Sima.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan had the personal name Yi and the courtesy name Zhongda. He came from Xiaojing Ward in Wen County, Henei Commandery, and belonged to the Sima clan.

units.zh: 晉國初建，追尊曰宣王。

translations.literal: When Jin state first founded posthumously honored King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raised him King Xuan.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，上尊號曰宣皇帝，陵曰高原，廟稱高祖。

translations.literal: When Wu-di accepted abdication elevated honorific Emperor Xuan—mausoleum Gaoyuan—temple styled Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he raised the honorific Emperor Xuan; the mausoleum was Gaoyuan; the temple name was Gaozu.

units.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」

translations.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'
translations.idiomatic: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."

units.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。

translations.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

units.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。

translations.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

notes: Both records use the full personal name 趙倫 (Zhao Lun) and are attested as Jin rebels in AD 301; the Jinshu alternate 司馬倫 does not contradict the shared name.

title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二: 高祖下
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二: 高祖下 Volume 2: Emperor Wu 2

units.zh: 梁德不造，喪亂積年，東夏崩騰，西都蕩覆。
units.literal: Liang's virtue was unmade; mourning and disorder piled up for years. The eastern domains collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was swept away.
units.idiomatic: Liang's mandate failed; mourning and chaos lasted for years. The east erupted in rebellion; the western capital was overrun.

units.zh: 蕭勃干紀，非唯趙倫，侯景滔天，踰於劉載。
units.literal: Xiao Bo defied the statutes—he was not merely Zhao Lun. Hou Jing reached to Heaven—he surpassed Liu Zai.
units.idiomatic: Xiao Bo rebelled against the throne—his crime outdid Zhao Lun's. Hou Jing's outrage touched Heaven—it exceeded Liu Zai's.

units.zh: 貞陽反篡，賊約連兵，江左累屬於鮮卑，金陵久非於梁國。
units.literal: Zhenyang turned traitor and usurped; the bandits' pact linked armies. The lands east of the Yangtze long belonged to the Xianbei; Jinling for long was no longer the land of Liang.
units.idiomatic: Zhenyang seized the throne by treachery; rebels joined forces in league. The lands east of the Yangtze fell under Xianbei rule; Jinling for long was no longer Liang's.

title.zh: 卷三十二 列傳第二 后妃下
title.en: Volume 32 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts Part Two
title.raw: 卷三十二 列傳第二 后妃下 Volume 32 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts Part Two

units.zh: 宣穆閱禮，偶德潛鱗，翊天造之艱虞，嗣塗山之逸響，寶運歸其後胤，蓋有母儀之助焉。
units.literal: Xuanmu examined rites; paired virtue hidden fish-scale; assisted Heaven-making's hardship and anxiety; continued Tushan's lingering echo; precious fortune returned to her later descendants—probably had motherly model's assistance.
units.idiomatic: Empress Xuanmu mastered ritual and matched her lord while he still hid like a dragon in the deep; she steadied him through peril and echoed the virtue of Tushan—later triumph rested with her line in part because she showed what a mother of the state should be.

units.zh: 武元楊氏預聞朝政，明不逮遠，愛溺私情，深杜衛瓘之言，不曉張泓之詐，運其陰沴，韜映乾明，晉道中微，基于是矣。
units.literal: Lady Yang of Wuyuan participated in hearing dynastic government; brightness did not reach far; love drowned in private feeling; deeply blocked Wei Guan's words; did not comprehend Zhang Hong's deceit; wielded her sinister balefulness; concealed and dimmed Qian brightness; Jin's path waned in the middle—the foundation lay herein.
units.idiomatic: Lady Yang of Wuyuan meddled in state affairs: foresight failed her, partial love swayed her, she silenced Wei Guan and never saw through Zhang Hong—the poison she spread dimmed the imperial house, and the decline of Jin began there.

units.zh: 惠皇稟質，王縱其嚚，識暗鳴蛙，智昏文蛤。
units.literal: Emperor Hui received substance; consorts of Wang indulged their viciousness; insight dark as croaking frogs; wisdom dim as patterned clams.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui was dull by nature while the Wang women unleashed their malice—his wit was no brighter than a frog's croak, his judgment no sharper than a clam in mud.

units.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
units.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
units.idiomatic: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

units.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
units.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
units.idiomatic: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

units.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
units.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
units.idiomatic: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第五十 王羲之 Volume 80 Biographies 50: Wang Xizhi

units.zh: 後之覽者，亦將有感於斯文。
units.literal: Later viewers, also will have feeling toward this text.
units.idiomatic: Readers who come after us may yet find something of themselves in these lines.

units.zh: 或以潘岳《金穀詩序》方其文，羲之比于石崇，聞而甚喜。
units.literal: Some with Pan Yue's "Jingu Poems Preface" compared his text; Xizhi compared to Shi Chong, hearing was greatly pleased.
units.idiomatic: Some likened his piece to Pan Yue's preface to the Golden Valley poems and compared Wang Xizhi himself to Shi Chong; he was delighted to hear it.

units.zh: 性愛鵝，會稽有孤居姥養一鵝，善鳴，求市未能得，遂攜親友命駕就觀。
units.literal: By nature loved geese; Kuaiji had an old woman living alone raising one goose, good at crying; seeking to buy could not obtain; then carrying kin and friends ordered carriage to go view.
units.idiomatic: He adored geese. An old widow in Kuaiji kept one with a fine voice; he tried to buy it without success, so he brought friends and rode out to see it.

units.literal: Chao said: "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen and Xu of Wei, Pan and Lu of Jin."
units.idiomatic: Lü Chao said, "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen Lin and Xu Gan of Wei, Pan Yue and Lu Ji of Jin."

units.literal: At the beginning of Jin Emperor Hui's reign, Wei Guan was Grand Guardian.
units.idiomatic: At the start of Jin Huidi's reign, Wei Guan was made Grand Guardian.

units.idiomatic: Thereafter no one held Grand Preceptor; Grand Guardian survived only as a posthumous grant.
